This PR enhances the fixes the existing search functionality on the companies table with technology and region.

## Changes Made:

### JavaScript (companies-table.js):
- Fixed search algorithm to check `companyTechnologies` and `region` fields, which were already merged previously to the main branch.

## Technical Details:

**Before:**
```javascript
var companyName = company.nameText.toLowerCase();
if (companyName.includes(searchValue)) {
	exactMatchResults.push({ ref: index });
}
```
**After:**
```javascript
var companyName = company.nameText.toLowerCase();
var companyTech = company.companyTechnologies ? company.companyTechnologies.toLowerCase() : '';
var region = company.region ? company.region.toLowerCase() : '';
if (companyName.includes(searchValue) || companyTech.includes(searchValue) || region.includes(searchValue)) {
	exactMatchResults.push({ ref: index });
}
```
## Benefits:
- Users can now search by technology stack (e.g., "React", "React Native", "Python")
- Users can filter companies by region (e.g., "Worldwide", "Europe", "US")
- No breaking changes to existing functionality

author: ryantxu
body:
**What is this feature?**
This allows using the DataQuery object from pluigns-sdk inside an app platform resource


**Why do we need this feature?**
Without registering this function, the apiequality functions (used to check if a resource has changed at all) will fail:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.24.17/third_party/forked/golang/reflect/deep_equal.go#L232

Specifically, the QueryLibrary feature needs this -- but given that it depends on such a core component (a query!) it seems better if we fix it for everyone who may add a query to a resource rather than just QueryLibrary.

**Who is this feature for?**

Grafana developers. Speciffically the QueryLibary service

body:
The "Cancel Coding Agent" button now shows a loading spinner during the cancellation process to provide clear visual feedback to users.

## Problem
Users reported that when clicking "Cancel Coding Agent", the button would become disabled for ~10 seconds with no visual indication that the cancellation was still in progress. This left users uncertain whether the action was working or if the button was stuck.

## Solution
Added a spinning loading icon that appears inline with the button text when the cancellation is in progress:

- **Before**: Button shows "Cancel Coding Agent" and becomes disabled (no visual feedback)
- **After**: Button shows "🔄 Cancel Coding Agent" with animated spinner while disabled

## Implementation Details
- Leverages existing `isBusy` state management in `CancelCodingAgentButton`
- Uses the existing `loadingIcon` component with CSS animations already present in the codebase
- Minimal changes to `ContextDropdown` interface to support React nodes in button labels
- Maintains backward compatibility - all existing dropdown buttons continue to work unchanged

## Technical Changes
1. Updated `ContextDropdownProps.defaultOptionLabel` to accept `string | React.ReactNode`
2. Modified `ContextDropdown` to safely handle React nodes in the title attribute
3. Enhanced `CancelCodingAgentButton` to conditionally show spinner when `isBusy` is true

The implementation provides immediate visual feedback that the cancellation is actively processing, improving the user experience during the 10-second operation.

Fixes #7451.

author: steffende
body:
So I splitted the AGENTS.md into a couple of smaller files. We also differentiate between generic Phoenix rules and rules specifically for new projects. The idea is that if you have an existing project, you can use something like `usage_rules` to get the generic rules from Phoenix (only the ones you need) and `phx.new` creates rules specifically tailored for the project.

We exclude rules based on `--no-ecto`, `--no-live` and `--no-html`.

When running `mix phx.gen.auth` we inject new auth rules into an existing `AGENTS.md` file (we should make this optional behind a flag). The injected text is based on the provided arguments. If someone does `mix phx.gen.auth Admins Admin admins` we talk about `current_scope.admin` etc.; When using the non-live version, text about live_sessions and other LiveView specifics is excluded.

This will probably interest @zachdaniel. I did not test it together with usage_rules yet. Is it supported to only have sub rules and no main `usage_rules.md`?

There another problem we need to solve. The generic rules live in `usage_rules/`, but we need to somehow copy them into the installer package before publishing to hex, otherwise the generic rules won't be available.

Added a new input property `wmMapPositionZoomCurrentLocation` to the `WmMapPositionDirective`. This property allows the map to automatically zoom in on the user's current location when set to `true`. A private method `_zoomInPosition` was also introduced to handle the zooming functionality.

- Added `wmMapPositionZoomCurrentLocation` input property.
- Implemented `_zoomInPosition` method to zoom the map to the user's current location.

author: majdyz
body:
## Summary
- Adds AI-generated activity status summaries for agent execution results
- Provides users with conversational, non-technical summaries of what their agents accomplished
- Includes comprehensive execution data analysis with honest failure reporting

## Changes Made
- **Backend**: Added `ActivityStatusGenerator` module with async LLM integration
- **Database**: Extended `GraphExecutionStats` and `Stats` models with `activity_status` field
- **Frontend**: Added "Smart Agent Execution Summary" display with disclaimer tooltip
- **Settings**: Added `execution_enable_ai_activity_status` toggle (disabled by default)
- **Testing**: Comprehensive test suite with 12 test cases covering all scenarios

## Key Features
- Collects execution data including graph structure, node relations, errors, and I/O samples
- Generates user-friendly summaries from first-person perspective
- Honest reporting of failures and invalid inputs (no sugar-coating)
- Payload optimization for LLM context limits
- Full async implementation with proper error handling

## Test Plan
- [x] All existing tests pass
- [x] New comprehensive test suite covers success/failure scenarios
- [x] Feature toggle testing (enabled/disabled states)
- [x] Frontend integration displays correctly
- [x] Error handling and edge cases covered

author: eveld
body:
## Problem

When HCL encounters configuration errors like unknown fields or blocks in wrong locations, hclconfig was producing misleading error messages that made debugging very difficult.

### Before this fix:
- Unknown field (e.g., `content` instead of `file`): 
  ```
  unable to create resource "resource.page.customize_homepage": read /path/to/lab: is a directory
  ```
- Block in wrong location (e.g., `check` at task level instead of condition level): Silent success ❌

### After this fix:
- Unknown field: 
  ```
  Missing required argument; The argument "file" is required, but no definition was found.
  ```
- Block in wrong location:
  ```
  Unsupported block type; Blocks of type "check" are not expected here.
  ```

## Root Cause

The issue was in `dag.go` lines 267-291. The `errorSummaries` list was missing two critical HCL error types:
- `"Unsupported attribute"` - for unknown fields
- `"Unsupported block type"` - for blocks placed at incorrect levels

This caused these errors to be treated as warnings instead of errors, leading to them being swallowed or converted to misleading messages.

## Solution

Added the missing error summaries to the `errorSummaries` list:
```go
errorSummaries := []string{
    // ... existing entries ...
    "Unsupported argument",
    "Unsupported attribute",      // ← Added
    "Unsupported block type",     // ← Added
}
```

## Testing

Verified the fix works by:
1. Building CLI with local hclconfig changes
2. Testing with invalid field name - now shows clear "Missing required argument" error
3. Testing with block in wrong location - now shows clear "Unsupported block type" error
4. Both scenarios previously showed misleading "is a directory" error or passed silently

## Impact

This significantly improves the debugging experience for users writing HCL configuration by providing clear, actionable error messages instead of confusing generic errors.

Discovered while testing the getting started guide where `content` was incorrectly used instead of `file` for page resources, and `check` blocks were placed at task level instead of condition level.

author: joeziminski
body:
Further to #74 this PR allows `sub-` and `ses-` labels to be alphanumeric, removing the requirement for these to be numeric only. It is still recommended that labels are (optionally zero-padded) integers increasing as each new subject / session is added, but this is no longer a fixed requirement.

thanks @glopesdev for the suggestion! It is nice to allow this level of flexibility if required.

This PR is a change to the spec so does not require tests nor further documentation. It will need to be handled on the datashuttle side and would make sense to merge this and a datashuttle PR that handles it at the same tiem.

author: timriley
body:
We were checking for an import namespace using a component `root_key`, which is a symbol, whereas the importer was expecting strings. This led to imported components only becoming available on a full boot, not when lazy loading properly (because the check for their namespace in the importer would always return false due to the type mismatch).

This will resolve https://github.com/hanami/hanami/issues/1529.

author: ickshonpe
body:
# Objective

`TextFont` has `from_font` and `from_font_size` constructors but is missing one for line height.

## Solution

* Added a `from_line_height` constructor function to `TextFont`.
* Also added `From<Handle<Font>>` and `From<LineHeight>` impls.

We could also add a `From<f32>` for font size but I thought it might be confusing. At some some point we want to add responsive text size support, can do it then.

author: jeremyandrews
body:
## Problem

GooseBot was causing noise on every PR with 404 errors due to using the deprecated Claude model `claude-3-sonnet-20240229`.

## Solution

This PR addresses issue #623 by:

### 1. Disabling Automatic Triggers
- Removed the `pull_request_target` trigger from `.github/workflows/goosebot_review.yml`
- Added explanatory comments referencing the issue
- Preserved the `workflow_dispatch` trigger for manual use when desired

### 2. Updating to Claude Sonnet 4
- Changed model from deprecated `claude-3-sonnet-20240229` to `claude-sonnet-4-20250514`
- Made the model configurable via `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` environment variable
- Updated the workflow to explicitly set the new model

### 3. Documentation Updates
- Updated memory bank to reflect the changes

## Result

✅ **No more automatic noise on every PR**  
✅ **GooseBot preserved for manual use** via GitHub Actions workflow dispatch  
✅ **Uses latest Claude Sonnet 4 model** for better performance  
✅ **Future-proofed** with configurable model selection  

## Manual Usage

GooseBot can still be used manually by:
1. Going to the Actions tab
2. Selecting "GooseBot PR Review" workflow
3. Clicking "Run workflow"
4. Entering the PR number and scope

## Files Changed

- `.github/workflows/goosebot_review.yml` - Disabled auto-triggers, updated model
- `.github/scripts/goosebot_review.py` - Updated to Claude Sonnet 4, made model configurable
- `memory-bank/activeContext.md` - Documented the fix

Fixes #623

author: schustmi
body:
## Describe changes
This PR implements retry behaviour for the Kubernetes orchestrator pod by using Kubernetes jobs instead of raw pods.

To enable this, this PR adds a few things:
- A new, much simpler DAG runner. This class runs a few threads that are processing/starting/monitoring nodes, instead of having a single thread per node, which then spins up/joins threads for new nodes that can be started after it finishes.
- Logic to reconstruct the DAG node state from the status in the ZenML database as well as the step jobs in the cluster. To make this work, the orchestrator pod also stores some information as annotations on the job that created it.

Deprecations/Removals:
- Now that the Kubernetes orchestrator is only using Jobs instead of raw pods for everything, there were quite a few settings attributes that are now unused and deprecated.
- The orchestrator pod does not stream logs from the step pods anymore.

body:
# fix: add session synchronization to apiLogin() to resolve session.user.org null issue ## Summary Fixed the root cause of why `session.user.org` was null in e2e tests after `apiLogin()` when it should have been populated for organization admin users. **Root Cause**: `apiLogin()` performed server-side authentication via direct API calls but bypassed NextAuth's client-side session synchronization mechanism. Regular login through the UI triggers `router.push(callbackUrl)` which causes the browser to refresh and synchronize the session state, while `apiLogin()` only made API calls without triggering this refresh. **Solution**: Added a session synchronization call (`await page.context().request.get("/api/auth/session")`) after authentication in `apiLogin()` to ensure the browser context has the updated session data containing organization information. **Impact**: This fix resolves the session synchronization gap for all 60+ e2e test files that use `apiLogin()`, ensuring consistent session state without requiring timing workarounds. ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] **Verify session synchronization works consistently**: Test the original failing scenario manually to confirm `session.user.org` is now populated correctly after `apiLogin()` - [ ] **Run broader e2e test coverage**: Execute multiple e2e tests that use `apiLogin()` to ensure no regressions were introduced by the session synchronization change - [ ] **Validate the approach**: Confirm that calling `/api/auth/session` endpoint actually triggers equivalent session synchronization to the `router.push(callbackUrl)` behavior in regular login flows - [ ] **Check for production impact**: Ensure the change doesn't negatively affect production authentication flows or introduce performance overhead **Recommended Test Plan**: 1. Run the original failing test: `yarn e2e apps/web/playwright/settings/upload-avatar.e2e.ts --grep "it can upload a organization logo image"` 2. Test a few other e2e files that use `apiLogin()`: `apps/web/playwright/i18n-routing.e2e.ts`, `apps/web/playwright/settings-admin.e2e.ts` 3. Manual verification: Create an org admin user in browser and verify `session.user.org` is populated on organization profile pages --- ### Diagram ```mermaid %%{ init : { "theme" : "default" }}%% graph TD A["apps/web/playwright/fixtures/users.ts

Organization logo test"]:::minor-edit C["packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts

Session synchronization"]:::context E["60+ e2e test files
using apiLogin()"]:::context A -->|"triggers session sync"| D A -->|"used by"| B A -->|"used by"| E C -->|"populates session.user.org"| D B -->|"now works without timing workaround"| C subgraph Legend L1[Major Edit]:::major-edit L2[Minor Edit]:::minor-edit L3[Context/No Edit]:::context end classDef major-edit fill:#90EE90 classDef minor-edit fill:#87CEEB classDef context fill:#FFFFFF ``` ### Notes - The test showed significant progress after the fix - it successfully navigated to the organization profile page (which was the original `session.user.org` issue) but failed later at a different UI element, confirming the session synchronization is working - This change affects a large number of e2e tests (60+ files), so thorough testing is recommended to catch any edge cases - The session synchronization approach mimics what happens in regular login without requiring page navigation that was causing timeout issues **Session**: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/49e01e8d902c4dfa8d94adfc6fe23f9f **Requested by**: @eunjae-lee

author: ckulka
body:
This PR stops changing the file ownership of the Baikal folder upon container start.

This used to be required to ensure local volumes on the host have the correct permissions set and that the user id of nginx/httpd can access them. Nowadays though, the recommended approach is user re-mapping, see https://docs.docker.com/engine/security/userns-remap/.

Only breaking change as it changes default behaviour. Functionality is still available and can be enabled if required.

author: copilot
body: Fixes an issue where front card images in the Octocat Memory game were not loading properly due to incorrect image paths. ## Problem The memory game was referencing front card images without the proper directory prefix, causing 404 errors when the browser tried to load images from the root directory instead of the `/img` directory. This resulted in broken/blank images when cards were flipped, making the game unplayable. ## Root Cause In the card creation template (line 792 of `memory.html`), front card images were being referenced as: ```html ``` This caused the browser to request images like `http://localhost:8000/topguntocat.png` instead of the correct path `http://localhost:8000/img/topguntocat.png`. ## Solution Updated the template to include the `img/` directory prefix: ```html ``` This ensures consistency with the back card image (`img/ghwp.png`) and allows all card images to load properly from the `/img` directory. ## Testing - Verified that all 19 unique Octocat images now load successfully (200 OK responses) - Confirmed that flipped cards display the correct Octocat characters - No more 404 errors in browser console - Game functionality works as expected ## Before/After **Before:** Flipped cards showed broken images due to 404 errors **After:** All card images load properly and display the intended Octocat characters ![Fixed memory game showing properly loaded Octocat image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7b4efeaa-fd4f-416a-8bd4-e02506b53b22) *This pull request was created as a result of the following prompt from Copilot chat.* > The Octocat Memory game has an issue with the image paths. The front card images aren't correctly pointing to the `/img` directory. The game tries to reference images like `boxertocat_octodex.png` directly, but they should be prefixed with `img/` like the back card image already is (`img/ghwp.png`). This fix will ensure that all card images load properly from the `/img` directory. --- 💬 Share your feedback on Copilot coding agent for the chance to win a $200 gift card! Click [here](https://survey.alchemer.com/s3/8343779/Copilot-Coding-agent) to start the survey.

author: lerman25
body:
This PR introduces a new time measurement abstraction: `rs_wall_clock`.
It provides high-precision, wall-clock time using c`lock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC)`, in **nanoseconds**, with helper conversions to milliseconds. Unlike `clock()`, which measures CPU time and is unreliable in multi-threaded or asynchronous environments, `rs_wall_clock` offers consistent and accurate wall time measurement. The goal is to fully deprecate and remove `clock()` usage across the codebase.

The `rs_wall_clock` utility includes:

- A struct for capturing timestamps: `rs_wall_clock`
- Nanosecond and millisecond types: `rs_wall_clock_ns_t`, `rs_wall_clock_ms_t`
- Helper functions: `rs_wall_clock_init()`, `rs_wall_clock_elapsed_ns()`, `rs_wall_clock_now_ns()`, and `rs_wall_clock_convert_ns_to_ms()`.

As a first step, rs_wall_clock has been integrated into `FT.PROFILE` time measurement.
Avoiding touching timeout handling and other time-sensitive logic, to minimize risk of unintended behavioral changes.

**Next Steps**
- Migrate remaining timespec-based code (e.g. timeout.h, GC timers) to use rs_wall_clock
- Consider replacing all ad hoc time measurements with the unified rs_wall_clock API
- Consider using CLOCK_MONOTONIC_COARSE in places where `ms` granulity is enough ([stackoverflow thread](CLOCK_MONOTONIC_COARSE))

author: ct3685
body:
## PR Title
Upgrade `next` to 14.2.30 to Resolve Critical Middleware Authorization Vulnerability

## Description
This PR updates the `next` package from version `14.2.5` to `14.2.30` across the `web`, `ui`, and `packages-answers/ui` packages. The primary motivation for this upgrade is to mitigate a **critical security vulnerability** identified as [GHSA-f82v-jwr5-mffw](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-f82v-jwr5-mffw), which allows for **authorization bypass in Next.js middleware**.

The vulnerability affects `next@14.2.12`, which was being pulled in as a **transitive dependency** via the `ui` package. This patch ensures that all directly declared versions of `next` in the workspace align to `14.2.30`, which includes the official fix for this issue.

### Security Risk Summary
- **Issue:** Authorization checks in middleware can be bypassed.
- **Impacted Versions:** All versions < `14.2.25` in the 14.x line.
- **Fix Version:** `14.2.25` (patched), this PR upgrades to `14.2.30` for extra buffer and stability.
- **Transitive Source:** `ui@1.0.0` dependency from [creative-eval](https://github.com/integralads/creative-eval.git)
- **Resolution:** Upgraded `next` version explicitly to override vulnerable transitive version.

### Additional Notes
- Does **not** include changes to `pnpm-lock.yaml`; runtime behavior validated via direct version bump in `package.json`.
- Related packages were reordered to reduce diff noise but are unchanged functionally.

author: viniciusdsmello
body:
# Add Programmatic Configuration Support for Tracing Decorators

## 🚀 Overview

This PR adds the ability to programmatically configure API keys and pipeline IDs for Openlayer tracing decorators, providing an alternative to environment variables for more flexible runtime configuration.

## 🎯 Problem

Previously, users could only configure tracing through environment variables:

```python
# Only option before this PR
os.environ["OPENLAYER_API_KEY"] = "your_api_key_here"
os.environ["OPENLAYER_INFERENCE_PIPELINE_ID"] = "your_pipeline_id_here"

@trace()
def my_function():
    return "result"
```

This approach had limitations:
- **No runtime flexibility** - configuration must be set before application startup
- **Multi-environment challenges** - difficult to switch between different API keys/pipeline IDs
- **Docker/containerization issues** - requires environment variable management in deployment
- **Testing complexity** - harder to mock or override configuration in tests

## ✨ Solution

Added a new `configure()` function that allows programmatic configuration with a clear precedence chain:

### 🔧 New `configure()` Function

```python
from openlayer.lib import configure, trace

# Configure once at application startup
configure(
    api_key="your_api_key_here",
    inference_pipeline_id="your_pipeline_id_here",
    base_url="https://custom.api.com/v1"  # Optional
)

# Use decorators normally - no environment variables needed
@trace()
def my_function():
    return "result"
```

### 📋 Configuration Precedence

1. **Highest**: Values passed directly to decorators (`@trace(inference_pipeline_id="specific")`)
2. **Medium**: Values set via `configure()` function
3. **Lowest**: Environment variables (maintains backward compatibility)

## 🎨 Key Features

### ✅ **Flexible Configuration Options**

```python
# Basic programmatic configuration
configure(
    api_key="your_api_key",
    inference_pipeline_id="your_pipeline_id"
)

# Per-decorator override
@trace()  # Uses configured default
def func1():
    pass

@trace(inference_pipeline_id="override_pipeline")  # Overrides default
def func2():
    pass

# Mixed approach (environment + programmatic)
os.environ["OPENLAYER_API_KEY"] = "env_key"
configure(inference_pipeline_id="programmatic_pipeline")
```

### ✅ **Runtime Configuration Changes**

```python
# Switch configurations at runtime
configure(api_key="dev_key", inference_pipeline_id="dev_pipeline")
run_development_tests()

configure(api_key="prod_key", inference_pipeline_id="prod_pipeline")  
run_production_workload()
```

### ✅ **Testing Support**

```python
# Easy mocking in tests
def test_my_function():
    configure(
        api_key="test_key",
        inference_pipeline_id="test_pipeline"
    )
    # Test with known configuration
    result = my_traced_function()
    assert result == expected_value
```

## 🛠 Technical Implementation

### **Enhanced Client Initialization**
- Modified `_get_client()` to use configured values with fallback to environment variables
- Client recreation when configuration changes (lazy initialization)
- Support for custom base URLs and SSL configuration

### **Pipeline ID Precedence Chain**
- Updated `_handle_trace_completion()` to implement proper precedence logic
- Maintained all existing functionality while adding new configuration options

### **Public API Integration**
- Added `configure` to public exports in `src/openlayer/lib/__init__.py`
- Comprehensive docstrings with usage examples

## 📝 Usage Examples

### **Multi-Environment Application**
```python
from openlayer.lib import configure

class MyApp:
    def __init__(self, environment: str):
        if environment == "development":
            configure(
                api_key=dev_config.openlayer_key,
                inference_pipeline_id=dev_config.pipeline_id
            )
        elif environment == "production":
            configure(
                api_key=prod_config.openlayer_key,
                inference_pipeline_id=prod_config.pipeline_id
            )
```

### **Dynamic Configuration**
```python
# Load from database, secrets manager, etc.
config = load_config_from_database()
configure(
    api_key=config.get("openlayer_api_key"),
    inference_pipeline_id=config.get("pipeline_id")
)
```

## ⚠️ Breaking Changes

**None** - This is a purely additive change that maintains full backward compatibility with existing environment variable usage.

## 🧪 Testing

- ✅ **9 new comprehensive tests** covering all configuration scenarios
- ✅ **Backward compatibility verified** - existing environment variable behavior unchanged
- ✅ **Integration tests** - verified existing tracing functionality still works
- ✅ **Precedence testing** - confirmed proper fallback chain behavior

### Test Coverage
```bash
python -m pytest tests/test_tracer_configuration.py -v
# ============================================ 9 passed in 7.78s ============================================
```

## 📁 Files Changed

- `src/openlayer/lib/tracing/tracer.py` - Added `configure()` function and enhanced client initialization
- `src/openlayer/lib/__init__.py` - Exported `configure` to public API
- `examples/tracing/programmatic_configuration.py` - Comprehensive usage examples
- `tests/test_tracer_configuration.py` - Full test suite covering all scenarios

## 🎉 Benefits

1. **🔄 Runtime Flexibility** - Change configuration without restarting applications
2. **🏗️ Better Architecture** - Cleaner separation of configuration from deployment
3. **🧪 Enhanced Testing** - Easier to mock and test different configurations  
4. **📦 Container-Friendly** - Reduces dependency on environment variable management
5. **🔒 Security** - Enables integration with secrets management systems
6. **⚡ Zero Disruption** - Existing code continues to work unchanged

## 📖 Documentation

Added comprehensive examples in `examples/tracing/programmatic_configuration.py` demonstrating:
- Environment variable approach (existing)
- Programmatic configuration (new)
- Per-decorator overrides
- Mixed configuration strategies

All functions include detailed docstrings with usage examples and parameter descriptions.

body:
This PR implements the `/export <world> [file]` command that allows users to export world configurations, agent details, and conversation history to markdown files.

## What this PR does

The new `/export` command provides a comprehensive way to backup and document world state:

```bash
# Export with auto-generated filename (world-timestamp.md)
/export my-world

# Export to custom file
/export my-world backup.md
```

## Implementation Details

### Command Structure
- **Usage**: `/export <world> [file]`
- **Parameters**: 
  - `world` (required): Name of the world to export
  - `file` (optional): Output file path, defaults to `[world]-timestamp.md` in current directory

### Export Content
The generated markdown includes:
- **World Configuration**: Name, ID, description, turn limit, agent count
- **Agent Details**: For each agent - configuration, LLM settings, system prompts, activity statistics
- **Conversation History**: Complete agent memory with timestamps, roles, and message content

### Example Output
```markdown
# World Export: my-world

**Exported on:** 2025-07-30T15:06:35.233Z

## World Configuration
- **Name:** my-world
- **ID:** my-world
- **Description:** A sample world
- **Turn Limit:** 10
- **Total Agents:** 2

## Agents (2)

### assistant-agent
**Configuration:**
- **LLM Provider:** openai
- **Model:** gpt-4
- **Status:** active

**Memory (3 messages):**
1. **user** (HUMAN)
   *2025-07-30T14:30:15.123Z*
   Hello, how can you help me?
```

## Key Features

- ✅ **Minimal Changes**: Only 3 files modified, leveraging existing infrastructure
- ✅ **Error Handling**: Graceful handling of non-existent worlds
- ✅ **CLI Integration**: Works in both pipeline and interactive modes
- ✅ **Help System**: Fully integrated with existing command documentation
- ✅ **Timestamp Support**: Automatic filename generation with ISO date format

## Testing

The implementation has been thoroughly tested:
- Default and custom filename generation
- Error scenarios (non-existent worlds)
- Both pipeline (`--command "/export world"`) and interactive modes
- Agent memory export with conversation history
- Help system integration (`/help export`)

This addresses the user requirement for a simple way to backup world state and provides a foundation for data portability between environments.

author: leosvelperez
body:
## Current Behavior

- The logic to detect whether the workspace uses the TS solution setup restricts the top-level properties in the `tsconfig.base.json` file and only allows `compilerOptions`. This prevents extending from other tsconfig files in the `tsconfig.base.json` file.
- Generating projects in a workspace without any known root tsconfig files (`tsconfig.json`, `tsconfig.base.json`) results in the old setup being generated. Workspaces without root TS configuration should be able to use the TS solution setup.

## Expected Behavior

- The logic to detect whether the workspace uses the TS solution should not restrict the top-level properties in the `tsconfig.base.json` file. The only things required for the TS solution setup are to have `composite: true` and `declarations` enabled.
- The TS solution setup should be used when generating projects in a workspace without any known root tsconfig files (`tsconfig.json`, `tsconfig.base.json`).

## Related Issue(s)

Fixes #32134

author: copilot
body:
The `FirmwareUpdateCoordinator` in the homeassistant_hardware integration was not passing the `config_entry` parameter to its parent `DataUpdateCoordinator` class, causing it to rely on ContextVar instead. This triggered a deprecation warning that will become an error in Home Assistant 2026.8:

```
Detected that integration 'homeassistant_hardware' relies on ContextVar, but should pass the config entry explicitly. at homeassistant/components/homeassistant_hardware/coordinator.py, line 29
```

## Changes Made

1. **Updated `FirmwareUpdateCoordinator`** to accept a `config_entry` parameter and pass it explicitly to the parent `DataUpdateCoordinator` constructor
2. **Updated integrations** that use `FirmwareUpdateCoordinator`:
   - `homeassistant_sky_connect` now passes `config_entry` when creating the coordinator
   - `homeassistant_yellow` now passes `config_entry` when creating the coordinator
3. **Updated test files** to match the new constructor signature using `MockConfigEntry`

## Technical Details

Before this fix, the coordinator relied on `config_entries.current_entry.get()` from ContextVar when no explicit config entry was provided. Now it receives the config entry explicitly, eliminating the ContextVar dependency.

The fix is minimal and surgical - only the parameter passing mechanism is updated to be explicit rather than relying on ContextVar. No existing functionality is affected.

Fixes #149681.

documentation.

## Motivation

The way we've designed and use most of the APIs is by passing transactions directly to EVM/block executors, thus using `IntoTxEnv` does not make perfect sense as it consumes `self` while we're mostly doing `&self -> TxEnv` conversions now.

## Solution

This PR introduces `BuildTxEnv` which takes `&self` and is automatically implemented for references. This allows to simplify some of the `TxEnv` implementations and drop `Copy` supertrait from `ExecutableTx`, allowing to pass owned transactions to block executors instead of just references.

The only `IntoTxEnv` implementations are now for `BuildTxEnv` and for `Self`

- [ ] Added Tests
- [ ] Added Documentation
- [ ] Breaking changes

## Problem

The `make test-all` command was failing during the test environment validation step due to an incorrect import name for the `pytest-xdist` package in the validation script.

**Error observed:**
```
❌ pytest-xdist: No module named 'pytest_xdist'
```

## Root Cause

In `scripts/validate_test_environment.py`, line 15 attempted to import `pytest_xdist`, but the correct module name for the pytest-xdist package is `xdist`, not `pytest_xdist`.

## Solution

Fixed the import name in the validation script from `'pytest_xdist'` to `'xdist'` to properly detect the pytest-xdist package installation.

**Change made:**
```python
# Before
('pytest_xdist', 'pytest-xdist'),

# After  
('xdist', 'pytest-xdist'),
```

This follows the standard pytest plugin naming convention where:
- Package name: `pytest-xdist` (used with `pip install`)
- Import name: `xdist` (used with `import` statements)

## Expected Outcome

After this fix:
- The `make test-all` command should pass the validation step
- All test dependencies will be correctly detected as available
- The test suite can run successfully with parallel execution via the `-n auto` flag

## Testing

- Validated that the script compiles without errors
- Confirmed the error message changed from "No module named 'pytest_xdist'" to "No module named 'xdist'"

This pull request refactors the real-time call handling logic in the `RecentCallsClient` component to simplify state management and improve the user experience. The most significant changes include removing redundant optimistic UI updates, relying on server-sent events (SSE) for real-time updates, and eliminating unnecessary background data refreshes.

### Refactoring of Call Handling Logic:
* Simplified the `handleViewNewCall` function by removing optimistic UI updates and background refresh logic. The function now resets filters and opens the call detail modal using SSE payload data. (`[app/recent-calls/RecentCallsClient.tsxL180-R193](diffhunk://#diff-be38862f98443ca42eb6e9d733d54c31e3d48b3e62bde54dd0b6e767507d47d8L180-R193)`)
* Replaced the optimistic UI update logic with a new SSE-based approach to immediately add new calls to the table. This ensures real-time updates without requiring revalidation. ### Removal of Redundant Code:
* Removed the background data refresh triggered after receiving new call data, as SSE data is now trusted for immediate updates. (`[app/recent-calls/RecentCallsClient.tsxL263-R254](diffhunk://#diff-be38862f98443ca42eb6e9d733d54c31e3d48b3e62bde54dd0b6e767507d47d8L263-R254)`)

### Changes Made

1. **Updated `IntegralProblem` constructor calls**
   - Changed `IntegralProblem(f, lb, ub, p)` to `IntegralProblem(f, (lb, ub), p)`

   - `IntegralProblem(f, domain, nout=n)` → `IntegralProblem(IntegralFunction(f, zeros(n)), domain)`

This change introduces render pipelines, an XML-configurable collection of render passes that draw meshes in a certain way.

The options at the moment are limited (alpha blending, depth sorting, etc), but this already allows transparent meshes to be properly drawn on top of solid meshes, instead of being arbitrarily drawn before or after. Most of the settings have been migrated from Materials.xml to the new RenderPipelines.xml. Materials.xml now define the shaders and shader parameters.

This concept can later be extended with post-processing steps and so on.

author: jacxk
body:
## Changes

- Added `/logs` endpoint for `/databases/{uuid}`
- Added `/logs` endpoint for `/services/{uuid}`, which requires a `sub_service_name` query parameter
- Added `show_timestamps` (bool) query params to display the logs timestamps 
	- #6287 

To get the database logs I just duplicated the `getCurrentServiceContainerStatus` and changed the filter to `coolify.databaseId`. Then, used the same logic as the application logs endpoint.

However, it was bit complicated to get the logs for a service. Explanation bellow.

##

A service can consist of multiple containers (sub-resources), such as databases and applications. Because of this, it's not practical to return all logs in a single response. Instead, the logs should be scoped to a specific endpoint, in this case a query filter.

I created helper function (derived from `getCurrentServiceContainerStatus`) to retrieve container information using the Docker label `coolify.name`. This label appears to uniquely identify individual sub-services within a service.

While implementing this, I considered using `coolify.service.subId` but noticed that multiple containers can share the same subId. Based on some testing, `coolify.name` remains consistent even when the user changes the display name in the UI, unlike `coolify.resourceName`, which does change.

The implementation filters containers by `coolify.name`, retrieves the matching container ID, and passes it to the `getContainerLogs` function to fetch logs for that specific container.

### Example

**Request:**
```
GET /api/v1/services/kok4o8ks8s0w04wkowkw8gw8/logs?sub_service_name=appwrite-console
```

**Response:**
```json
{
  "logs": "/docker-entrypoint.sh: /docker-entrypoint.d/ is not empty, will attempt to perform configuration\n/docker-entrypoint.sh: Looking for shell scripts in /docker-entrypoint.d/\n..."
}
```

**Missing `sub_service_name`:**
```json
{
  "message": "Sub service name is required."
}
```

**Invalid `sub_service_name`:**
```json
{
  "message": "Container not found."
}
```

author: therealaph
body:
In MacOS/AArch64 HotSpot, we have to deal with the fact that a thread must be in one of two modes: it either may write to code cache memory or it may execute (and read) code or data in it. A system call `pthread_jit_write_protect_np(int enabled)` changes from one to the other. Today, we change mode whenever making a transition from interpreter to VM. This means that we change mode a lot: experiments have shown that during `jshell` startup we change mode 4 million times. Other experiments have shown that we only needed to change mode 45 thousand times. This "eager" mode switching is perhaps too eager, and we'd be better off switching lazily. While the system call that changes mode is very fast, mode switching still amounts to about 100ms of startup time. Switching eagerly also means that some native calls (e.g. to do arithmetic) are disproportionately expensive, given that they have no need of mode switching at all. The approach in this PR is to defer transitioning from exec-but-don't-write mode (`WXExec`) to write-but-don't-exec mode (`WXWrite`) until we need to write. Instead of enabling `WXWrite` immediately, we switch to a mode called `WXArmedForWrite`. When in this mode, when we need to write into code memory we call `os_bsd_jit_exec_enabled(false)` to enable writing and then set the current mode to `WXWrite`. We mark all sites that we know will write to code memory with `MACOS_AARCH64_ONLY(os::thread_wx_enable_write());` Judicious placement of these markers, such as when entering patching code, means that we have a fairly small number of these. We also keep track (in thread-local storage) of the current state of `pthread_jit_write_protect_np` in order to avoid making the system call unnecessarily. It is possible that we have missed some sites where we do need to make a transition from write-protected to -enabled. While we haven't seen any in testing, we have a fallback path. An attempt to write into code memory triggers a `SIGILL` signal. A signal handler detects this, and if the current mode `WXArmedForWrite` it changes mode to write-enabled and returns. In addition, the handler "heals" the VM entry point so that next time the same point is entered (and for the rest of the lifetime of the VM) it will immediately transition to `WXWrite`. One other possibility remains: we could omit all of the `wx_enable_write` markers and use healing instead. We've experimented with this. It works well enough, but is rather crude, and it's better to be able to see where transitions take place. --------- ### Progress - [x] Change must be properly reviewed (1 review required, with at least 1 [Reviewer](https://openjdk.org/bylaws#reviewer)) - [x] Change must not contain extraneous whitespace - [x] Commit message must refer to an issue ### Issue * [JDK-8328306](https://bugs.openjdk.org/browse/JDK-8328306): AArch64: MacOS lazy JIT "write xor execute" switching (**Enhancement** - P4) ### Reviewers * [Dean Long](https://openjdk.org/census#dlong) (@dean-long - **Reviewer**) * [Andrew Dinn](https://openjdk.org/census#adinn) (@adinn - **Reviewer**) ### Contributors * Dean Long `` ### Reviewing

body:
### Feature: Implement Frontend-Only Private Vault for Journal Entries

**Fixes issue #70**

#### Summary

This pull request introduces a comprehensive **Private Vault** feature, allowing users to store sensitive journal entries in a secure, PIN-protected area within the application , leveraging `localStorage` and React Context to manage state.

#### Changes

**1. Core Vault Functionality:**
*   **PIN Management:** Added a new "Vault Settings" section in the **Settings** page where users can create and update their 4-digit PIN. The PIN is stored in `localStorage`.
*   **Private Entry Storage:** A list of private entry IDs is now managed in `localStorage` and synced with the `JournalContext`.
*   **New Components:**
    *   `PrivateVault.jsx`: A new page that serves as the main view for locked entries.
    *   `PinEntry.jsx`: A reusable component for PIN input.
    *   `PinConfirmModal.jsx`: A modal used to verify the user's PIN before performing sensitive actions.

**2. User Experience and Security Enhancements:**
*   **PIN Confirmation:** Users are now required to enter their PIN via a modal before they can move a public entry into the vault, preventing accidental locking.
*   **Context-Aware Navigation:** The app now tracks whether a user is navigating from the main journal or the private vault. This fixes a bug where the browser's back button would lead to the wrong page after viewing or editing a private entry.

#### How to Test This Feature

1.  **Set PIN:**
    *   Navigate to `/settings`.
    *   Create a 4-digit PIN in the "Vault Settings" section.

2.  **Lock an Entry:**
    *   Go to the main `/journal` page.

author: muhammad-othman
body:
<!--- Provide a general summary of your changes in the Title above -->

## Description
The current code loads the whole response stream in memory before start the unmarshalling process. This works for small payloads but may cause issues for large response payloads.
The `System.Formats.Cbor.CborReader` doesn't accept stream and requires in memory byte array for deserialization.

This PR adds `CborReaderProxy` that wraps `System.Formats.Cbor.CborReader` to support processing the stream in chunks without ever holding the whole payload in memory, feeding the chunks into `CborReader` and process them one by one.


The default `CborReader.ReadEndMap()`/`CborReader.ReadEndArray()` methods assume the full map is already present in the input buffer and cannot continue reading if the buffer ends in the middle of a container.
This means the reader will fail to advance if the next token is a container break (0xFF) but the start wasn't read into the current buffer (it was read in a previous part of the stream).

To support maps/arrays across multiple refills I did the following:
* Implement custom `ReadStartMap`, `ReadEndMap`, `ReadStartArray`, `ReadEndArray`.
* Detect and skip container break markers `0xFF` as needed.
* Added `_nestingStack` to track when reading a nested CBOR structure (e.g., an array of maps), and correctly match calls to `ReadStartMap` with `ReadEndMap`, and `ReadStartArray` with `ReadEndArray`.


## Motivation and Context
`#DOTNET-8252`

## Testing
* Added `CborReaderProxyTests.cs` to cover the new changes.
* Tested various `CloudWatch` and `SecretsManager` operations with CBOR.
* `DRY_RUN-4ff92fab-9e40-46cc-88d0-746023de37cf`.

body:
## 🚀 Motivação
Muribeca relatou um problema com alunos durante a etapa de validação do status de ausência de CPF, em que estudantes com CPF estavam sendo exibidos com o campo justSemCpf igual a 0 — valor que indica ausência não justificada. Esse campo, no entanto, deveria aparecer apenas para alunos sem CPF cadastrado.
## 🔧 Alterações Realizadas
Após análise do problema, foram observados dois pontos principais:  
- A evidência enviada se referia a alunos que, de fato, não possuíam CPF cadastrado;  
- O método de montagem do documento apresentava código repetido e interações desnecessárias.

Com isso, foram realizadas as seguintes melhorias:  
- Separação da lógica de montagem do objeto do estudante em uma função dedicada;  
- Adição de uma validação extra para verificar corretamente a ausência de CPF.

## 🛠️ Fluxo de Teste

🧪 Fluxo de Teste 1 (FT1):
```
1. Vá em Sagres nas Integrações ;
2. Remova a opção de exclusão de alunos sem CPF;
3. Selecione o mês de Julho;
4. Gere o documento;
5. Baixe o zip;
6. Abra o zip em um editor de código;
7. Faça uma busca pela tag <justSemCpf> com o valor 0 Ex:"<justSemCpf>0"
8. Verifique se quando essa tag existir não exite cpf no registro do Aluno
```
✅ Sucesso: 
 - Não existe tag <justSemCpf> e <cpf> no mesmo registro de aluno
❌ Falha: 
 - Existe tag <justSemCpf> e <cpf> no mesmo registro de aluno

## Summary
Adds `uv.lock` file for deterministic dependency resolution and updates entire build pipeline to use locked dependencies for reproducible builds across all environments.

## Key Changes
- **Lock file**: Added `uv.lock` and `.python-version`, removed from `.gitignore`
- **Build system**: Updated Dockerfiles to use `uv sync --frozen` with optimized caching
- **Project structure**: Moved `/registry` → `/packages/tracecat-registry` for workspace compatibility
- **CI/CD**: Upgraded to uv 0.8.4, added frontend CI workflow, updated all workflows to use lock file
- **Pre-commit**: Added uv hooks for automatic lock file maintenance
- **Documentation**: Updated CLAUDE.md with uv workflow and template best practices

## Why?
Prevents dependency version mismatches between environments that could cause tests to pass locally but fail in CI, or production builds to behave differently than development.

## Dependency Updates
```bash
# Update specific package
uv lock --upgrade-package <package-name>

# Update all dependencies  
uv lock --upgrade && uv sync
```

body:
Removes two forgotten debug print statements that were causing excessive verbose output during EisensteinBasis computation.

## Issue
When running the test `Tests/cubic_eisenstein_fix.m`, users encountered verbose output with repeated patterns like:
```
1 Rational Field
Rational Field
-4 Rational Field
Rational Field
-12 Rational Field
...
```

## Root Cause
Two debug print statements were left in production code within nested loops:

1. **ModFrmHilD/Components.m:512** - In the `HMFComponent` intrinsic:
   ```magma
   print coeff, Parent(coeff), CoefficientRing;
   ```
   This was printing coefficient values, their parent field ("Rational Field"), and the coefficient ring during Fourier coefficient processing.

2. **ModFrmHilD/Trace/Trace.m:1042** - In the `HeckeTraceForm` intrinsic:
   ```magma
   print Norm(nn), Trace( HeckeOp(Mk,nn) );
   ```
   This was printing norms and traces during Hecke operator computations.

## Solution
Removed both debug print statements while preserving all computational logic. The functions now execute silently as intended, maintaining identical mathematical behavior without the unwanted output.

Fixes #474.

body:
## Problem

Three critical issues were addressed in this PR:

1. **Player settings not applying dynamically**: Settings (network buffer, hardware acceleration, stream format) were hardcoded and not applying dynamically. Users had to restart the app for settings changes to take effect.

2. **Verbose image loading logs**: The ImageLoader was producing excessive debug logs in all builds, including release builds, creating log noise with messages like "🏗 Cancelled" and "☁️ Successful (NETWORK)".

3. **VLC initialization crashes**: Invalid VLC options were causing LibVLC to fail initialization with `IllegalStateException: can't create LibVLC instance`.

## Root Causes

- **Hardcoded VLC options**: All ViewModels used fixed `arrayListOf("--network-caching=3000", "--file-caching=3000")`
- **Settings ignored**: Preferences were saved but never read when initializing VLC
- **No dynamic updates**: Changes required app restart to apply
- **Excessive logging**: Debug logs appeared in all builds causing log noise
- **Invalid VLC options**: Options like `--android-audio-session-id=0`, `--android-display-chroma=RV16`, and `--adaptive-logic=highest` don't exist in LibVLC

## Solution

### 1. Dynamic VLC Options Generation
Added `PreferenceManager.getVLCOptions()` that generates valid options based on current settings:

```kotlin
fun getVLCOptions(): ArrayList<String> {
    val options = arrayListOf<String>()
    
    // Apply network buffer (LOW=1000ms, MEDIUM=3000ms, HIGH=5000ms, ULTRA=8000ms)
    val bufferValue = when (getNetworkBuffer()) {
        "LOW" -> "1000"
        "MEDIUM" -> "3000" 
        "HIGH" -> "5000"
        "ULTRA" -> "8000"
        else -> "3000"
    }
    options.add("--network-caching=$bufferValue")
    options.add("--file-caching=$bufferValue")
    
    // Apply hardware acceleration
    if (getHwAcceleration()) options.add("--avcodec-hw=any")
    else options.add("--avcodec-hw=none")
    
    // Stream format optimizations
    when (getStreamFormat()) {
        "HLS" -> options.add("--http-reconnect")
        "TS" -> options.add("--ts-seek-percent")
    }
    
    // Performance improvements
    options.add("--audio-time-stretch")
    
    return options
}
```

### 2. Fixed Invalid VLC Options
Removed unsupported options that were causing crashes:
- ❌ `--android-audio-session-id=0` (doesn't exist in LibVLC)
- ❌ `--android-display-chroma=RV16` (Android-specific, not supported)
- ❌ `--adaptive-logic=highest` (invalid option)

### 3. Updated All Player ViewModels
- **MovieDetailsViewModel**: Uses dynamic options in `startPlayback()`
- **SeriesDetailsViewModel**: Uses dynamic options in episode playback  
- **ChannelsViewModel**: Uses dynamic options in `setupVLC()` and channel selection

### 4. Live Settings Updates
Added `updatePlayerSettings()` methods to recreate media with new options for immediate application.

### 5. Settings Change Notifications
Enhanced `SettingsViewModel` to emit `PlayerSettingsChanged` events when settings are modified.

### 6. Conditional Debug Logging
Modified `MainApplication.kt` to only enable ImageLoader debug logging in debug builds:

```kotlin
.apply {
    if (BuildConfig.DEBUG) {
        logger(DebugLogger())
    }
}
```

## Benefits

- ✅ **No more crashes**: VLC initializes successfully with valid options only
- ✅ **Immediate application**: Settings take effect instantly without restart
- ✅ **Better performance**: Users can optimize buffer sizes for their network
- ✅ **Hardware flexibility**: Hardware acceleration can be toggled based on device capabilities  
- ✅ **Stream optimization**: Format-specific optimizations improve playback quality
- ✅ **Cleaner logs**: Debug logs only appear in debug builds, eliminating release build noise
- ✅ **Maintainable**: Centralized VLC options logic eliminates code duplication

The implementation maintains backward compatibility while providing stable VLC initialization, immediate settings application, and cleaner logging for improved user experience.

Buildah versions <= 1.38.0 did not push all the images contained in a
multi-arch Manifest, only the manifest itself. The Ubuntu runners
we are using are shipping Buildah 1.33, so we need to explicitly set
`--all` when pushing the Manifest to ensure all images it contains are
pushed.

The individual images in our multi-arch plugin manifests were missing
the proper `ghcr.io/openbao` prefix. They are added by their SHA Hash to
the Manifest, so this did not impact functionality. It's just a cosmetic
change so you can see all the individual images with the correct tag if
you build locally.

body: I noticed that our replays w/ feedbacks have gaps while the user is entering in their feedback. This is because we call `replay.flush` (not to be confused w/ the public replay integration integration which also has a flush) which only flushes the buffer and continues to buffer. author: dwertent
body:
### Overview

This PR introduces support for a new `paladinNodeCount` configuration option in the Helm chart, allowing separate control over the number of Paladin and Besu nodes.

This is particularly useful for optimizing deployments in constrained environments (e.g., CI pipelines), where running multiple Besu nodes may be unnecessary or too resource-intensive.

This PR also adds a CI test to validate the `nodeCount` and `paladinNodeCount` configurations during installation. The test is integrated into the Gradle-based test suite to ensure both symmetric and asymmetric node setups deploy successfully.

Resolves: #756

### Updated Node Configuration

The chart now supports flexible node deployment through the following parameters:

#### Default Mode (Symmetric)

```yaml
nodeCount: 3  # Deploys 3 Paladin nodes + 3 Besu nodes (1:1 mapping)
```

#### Resource-Optimized Mode (Asymmetric)

```yaml
paladinNodeCount: 5  # Deploys 5 Paladin nodes + 1 Besu node
```

> When `paladinNodeCount` is set, the besuNodeCount automatically defaults to 1.

#### Node Connectivity

* **Single Besu Node**: All Paladin nodes connect to `besu-node1`
* **Multiple Besu Nodes**: Each Paladin node connects to a corresponding Besu node (1:1)

author: molly-moen
body:
I noticed sometimes my project in Python Lab/Web Lab 2 had no "active" file despite having open files. This was because if you deleted the active file, we weren't properly updating another file to be "active". This wasn't very noticeable because our logic for showing a file in the editor would fall back to the first open file if there was no active file, but did cause some weirdness with the current html file preview, since it relies on active files.

To fix this, I applied the same logic we use when closing an active file to deleting a file. I updated that logic a bit to use the `openFiles` list to decide which file to activate next, rather than sorting the files. I think the sorting was from a time when we didn't allow rearranging the file tabs in the editor. Now we can open the next file in the editor rather than the next file alphabetically.

If the user deletes an entire folder, we just go to the first open file, since multiple open files could have been deleted.

## Testing story
Tested locally and updated unit tests.

    pred = torch.full((1,1,2,2), 5.0)
    target = torch.ones((1,2,2))
    codeflash_output = lovasz_hinge_loss(pred, target); loss = codeflash_output # 67.1μs -> 53.7μs (25.0% faster)

def test_incorrect_shape_pred_raises():
    # pred has wrong shape
    pred = torch.ones((1,2,3,3))  # should be (B,1,H,W)
    target = torch.ones((1,3,3))
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        lovasz_hinge_loss(pred, target) # 226μs -> 221μs (2.07% faster)

def test_incorrect_shape_target_raises():
    # target has wrong shape
    pred = torch.ones((1,1,3,3))
    target = torch.ones((1,1,3,3))  # should be (B,H,W)
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        lovasz_hinge_loss(pred, target) # 117μs -> 118μs (0.847% slower)

def test_mismatched_hw_raises():
    # pred and target H,W mismatch
    pred = torch.ones((1,1,4,3))
    target = torch.ones((1,3,3))
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        lovasz_hinge_loss(pred, target) # 4.75μs -> 4.71μs (0.892% faster)


def test_non_binary_target():
    # target contains values other than 0 or 1
    pred = torch.ones((1,1,2,2))
    target = torch.tensor([[[0, 1], [2, 0]]])
    # Should not raise, but loss may be nonsensical
    codeflash_output = lovasz_hinge_loss(pred, target); loss = codeflash_output # 80.5μs -> 64.2μs (25.4% faster)

def test_empty_batch():
    # Batch size 0
    pred = torch.empty((0,1,2,2))
    target = torch.empty((0,2,2))
    with pytest.raises(Exception):
        lovasz_hinge_loss(pred, target) # 130μs -> 125μs (4.02% faster)

# ------------------------
# 3. Large Scale Test Cases
# ------------------------

def test_large_batch_and_image():
    # Large batch and image (but <1000 elements per dim)
    B, H, W = 16, 32, 32  # 16*32*32 = 16K pixels per batch
    pred = torch.randn((B,1,H,W))
    target = torch.randint(0,2,(B,H,W))
    codeflash_output = lovasz_hinge_loss(pred, target); loss = codeflash_output # 811μs -> 766μs (5.84% faster)

def test_large_all_correct():
    # Large input, all predictions correct
    B, H, W = 8, 64, 16
    pred = torch.full((B,1,H,W), 10.0)
    target = torch.ones((B,H,W))
    codeflash_output = lovasz_hinge_loss(pred, target); loss = codeflash_output # 157μs -> 111μs (40.9% faster)

def test_large_all_wrong():
    # Large input, all predictions wrong
    B, H, W = 8, 64, 16
    pred = torch.full((B,1,H,W), -10.0)
    target = torch.ones((B,H,W))
    codeflash_output = lovasz_hinge_loss(pred, target); loss = codeflash_output # 152μs -> 106μs (43.7% faster)

def test_large_randomized():
    # Large randomized input
    B, H, W = 10, 20, 40
    pred = torch.randn((B,1,H,W))
    target = torch.randint(0,2,(B,H,W))
    codeflash_output = lovasz_hinge_loss(pred, target); loss = codeflash_output # 426μs -> 382μs (11.4% faster)

def test_loss_meaningful_on_varied_batch():
    # Loss should be lower when predictions are more correct
    B, H, W = 4, 32, 32
    # First half: correct, second half: wrong
    pred = torch.cat([
        torch.full((B//2,1,H,W), 10.0),      # correct
        torch.full((B//2,1,H,W), -10.0)      # wrong
    ], dim=0)
    target = torch.cat([
        torch.ones((B//2,H,W)),
        torch.ones((B//2,H,W))
    ], dim=0)
    codeflash_output = lovasz_hinge_loss(pred, target); loss = codeflash_output # 117μs -> 81.8μs (44.0% faster)

author: alexander-sol
body:
Using a timsTOF, it is possible to generate data without using the tims for ion mobility separation. When this is done, it produces a different file type, where the .d folder contains .tsf and .tsf_bin files. 

Opening and interpreting these files requires different functions to be imported from the timsData.dll, as well as different processing logic. 

This PR extends the timsTOF file reader to access these files, and creates a new derived class, TsfFrameProxy, to handle data reading.

author: apricotppp
body:
This change was made to improve build compatibility with AOSP

STDC_FORMAT_MACROS is predefined in the AOSP build environment. Therefore, the #define __STDC_FORMAT_MACROS needs to be removed from each individual .cc file to the CMakeLists.txt file. 

Since AOSP build does not use CMakeLists,txt, this change will prevent the compiling errors of macro redefinition.

author: yashpatil641
body:
## Ticket

[Issue 33 ](https://github.com/agency-fund/evidential-sprint/issues/33)

## Description
This PR introduces a validation check to ensure the uniqueness of participant IDs for pre-assigned experiments. If participant IDs are not unique after filtering, experiment results can be biased. This change prevents such experiments from being created by raising an error early in the process.

The uniqueness check is performed in-memory on the filtered list of participants *before* they are passed to the `assign_treatment` function.

## Future Tasks (optional)

## How has this been tested?
A new unit test, `test_create_preassigned_experiment_impl_raises_on_duplicate_ids`, has been added to `src/xngin/apiserver/routers/experiments/test_experiments_common.py`.

This test confirms that the implementation correctly raises the expected `LateValidationError` when provided with a list of participants containing duplicate IDs.

body:
## Add C Bindings for Caliptra MCU Emulator

This PR introduces comprehensive C bindings for the Caliptra MCU Emulator, enabling C applications to control the emulator with full feature parity to the Rust implementation.

### Key Features Added:
- **Complete C API**: Full emulator control from C code with memory management handled by the C application
- **Real-time UART streaming**: Live UART output display and console input handling with raw terminal mode support
- **GDB integration**: Built-in GDB server support for debugging from C applications
- **Static library distribution**: Easy integration into existing C projects via `libemulator_cbinding.a`
- **External peripheral access**: Added `caliptra_to_ext_bus` to support external peripheral access for the emulator
- **Cross-platform support**: Linux, macOS, and Windows compatibility (x86_64, aarch64)

### Technical Implementation:
- Zero modifications to existing Rust emulator code required to implement a C emulator
- Type-safe C interface with proper error handling
- Configurable memory layout parameters with sensible defaults
- Thread-safety documentation and guidelines
- Complete command-line argument compatibility with Rust emulator
- External shim layer for peripheral integration

### New Components:
- cbinding crate with C bindings
- External shim for peripheral access support
- Auto-generated C header file (`emulator_cbinding.h`)
- Example C application demonstrating full functionality
- Build system integration with Make and cbindgen

This enables C/C++ projects to embed the Caliptra MCU Emulator directly while maintaining all original functionality including instruction tracing, manufacturing mode, hardware version configuration, and external peripheral access capabilities.

body:
Solves NullReferenceException caused by the ItemReceived handler not yet being registered if a save had not yet been loaded, since Disconnect() will unconditionally try to unregister it.

This fix means that if you become disconnected on the title screen, you can now reconnect

* api-change:``cloudfront``: [``botocore``] This release adds new origin timeout options: 1) ResponseCompletionTimeout and 2) OriginReadTimeout (for S3 origins)

* api-change:``ds``: [``botocore``] This release adds support for AWS Managed Microsoft AD Hybrid Edition, introducing new operations: StartADAssessment, DescribeADAssessment, ListADAssessments, DeleteADAssessment, CreateHybridAD, UpdateHybridAD, and DescribeHybridADUpdate; and updated existing operation: DescribeDirectories.

* api-change:``directconnect``: [``botocore``] Enable MACSec support and features on Interconnects.

* enhancement:``sso``: [``botocore``] Updates legacy token auth flow to check if cached legacy tokens are expired according to the local clock. If expired, it will raise an ``UnauthorizedSSOTokenError`` instead of sending an expired token to Identity Center's ``GetRoleCredentials`` API.

   ```
   =======

* api-change:``appintegrations``: [``botocore``] Amazon AppIntegrations introduces new configuration capabilities to enable customers to manage iframe permissions, control application refresh behavior (per contact or per browser/cross-contact), and run background applications (service).

* api-change:``config``: [``botocore``] Documentation improvements have been made to the EvaluationModel and DescribeConfigurationRecorders APIs.
* api-change:``ec2``: [``botocore``] Transit Gateway native integration with AWS Network Firewall. Adding new enum value for the new Transit Gateway Attachment type.
* api-change:``kms``: [``botocore``] Doc only update: fixed grammatical errors.
